title: Clay and its names
devanagari: यथा सोम्यैकेन मृत्पिण्डेन सर्वं मृन्मयं विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
iast: yathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛnmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttikety eva satyam
english: “Just as, my dear, by one piece of clay everything made of clay may be known—the modification is merely a verbal distinction, a name; the reality is just ‘clay’—”
translator: Robert Ernest Hume, The Thirteen Principal Upanishads (Oxford University Press, 1921)
edition: Sanskrit: Chāndogya Upaniṣad, Sansknet project input, as on GRETIL
notes: Uddālaka is teaching his son Śvetaketu, who has come home proud of his learning. A water jar, a bowl and a lamp are different names and shapes, and each is useful as what it is. What they are made of is one thing: clay.
